summary: Spain is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (with the ETIAS travel authorisation being phased in), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa costing €90.

fee.notes: Children 6–11: €45; under 6: free. Fee set EU-wide since 11 June 2024.
For stays over 90 days: residence, family reunification and other long-stay purposes. Fee varies by nationality due to reciprocity.
Required for courses longer than 90 days; needs proof of enrolment, funds and health insurance.
For remote workers employed by non-Spanish companies; income requirement of roughly 200% of the Spanish minimum wage.
Requires a work authorisation obtained by the employer in Spain before the visa application.

passportValidity.text: Non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen Area and have been issued within the last 10 years.

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it but border officers may ask about cover.

onwardTicket.text: Border officers may ask non-EU visitors for proof of return or onward travel and accommodation details.

proofOfFunds.text: Spain sets a minimum means requirement for non-EU visitors: roughly €118 per person per day, with a minimum total around €1,065 per trip (figures are updated annually).

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travellers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border — there is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorisation System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travellers will need an ETIAS travel authorisation to enter the Schengen Area. It is being phased in — check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: Duty-free from outside the EU: 200 cigarettes, 1 litre of spirits, goods up to €300 (€430 arriving by air/sea).
No limits on goods for personal use when arriving from another EU country.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments are accepted almost everywhere, including small purchases. Some small bars and markets remain cash-only.

safety.text: Spain is one of Europe's safest destinations. The main risk for visitors is pickpocketing in tourist hotspots of Madrid and Barcelona.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Spain Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: April–June and September–October offer warm weather without the peak-summer heat and crowds; the south is pleasant even in winter.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Spain — days spent in France or Italy count against the same allowance.
First-time EES biometric registration can add queue time at airports — arrive with margin on your first Schengen entry.
Apply for ETIAS only at the official travel-europe.europa.eu site once it becomes mandatory — unofficial sites charge inflated fees.
Keep valuables secure on the Madrid and Barcelona metro and around major sights — pickpocketing is the most common tourist crime.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Spain?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Spain and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, they will need to obtain this online authorisation (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Spain Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Spain?
faq.answer: ETIAS is being phased in for visa-exempt travellers. During the transition period travellers without ETIAS are still admitted; once fully mandatory, the €20 online authorisation will be required before boarding. Check the official EU website for the current status.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Spain?
faq.answer: It is mandatory for Schengen visa applicants: medical cover of at least €30,000 valid throughout the Schengen Area. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to present insurance, though it is strongly recommended.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Spain without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area. EU and EFTA citizens can stay indefinitely but must register locally after 3 months.
